stories.title: Change my password securely
stories.story: As a user, I want password changes to require my current password, so that a stolen session cannot take over my account.
tasks: Ask for current password; fix false 'updated' message on failure
Turn on Secure password change in the Supabase dashboard (live)

### What
Turn on the Secure password change setting on the live Supabase project.

### Why
`config.toml` has `secure_password_change = true`, but that file only affects the local stack. Until this is on live, a stolen session can change the password without the current one (SEC-21).

### Where
- Supabase dashboard → Authentication → Email → Secure password change

### Steps
1. Open the live project in the Supabase dashboard.
2. Authentication → Email: turn on Secure password change and save.
3. In the app: Settings → Change Password with a wrong current password, then with the right one.

### Done when
- [ ] Setting is on in the live project
- [ ] Wrong current password is refused, right one works

### What
Run the change-password Maestro flow against a build that has the new Current Password field.

### Why
The flow was updated for the re-authentication change (current password + confirm-identity) but has never been run.

### Where
- `maestro/change-password.yaml`
- `maestro/subflows/confirm-identity.yaml` (test PIN 1234)

### Steps
1. Do the live dashboard switch first (Secure password change).
2. Boot an emulator/simulator with a current dev build.
3. `maestro test maestro/change-password.yaml`
4. Fix any selector drift, re-run until green.

### Done when
- [ ] Flow passes on Android
- [ ] Flow passes on iOS (or the iOS gap is written down)

stories.title: Delete my account without breaking others' chats
stories.story: As a user, I want to delete my account and data, so that I leave no trace, while other members keep their group chats (SEC-12).
tasks: `delete-account` removes only the caller's rows, keeps groups with members
Apply `20261026000100` and `20261026000200` migrations to the live project

### What
Apply the two pending migrations to the live database: drop `profiles.fcm_token` (SEC-13) and drop the `conversations.created_by` foreign key (SEC-12).

### Why
Without the FK drop, `delete-account` cannot keep a group whose creator leaves, and the old `fcm_token` column leaks stale tokens to every user.

### Where
- `supabase/migrations/20261026000100_drop_profiles_fcm_token.sql`
- `supabase/migrations/20261026000200_conversations_created_by_no_fk.sql`

### Steps
1. Optional check first: `select count(*) from public.profiles where fcm_token is not null;`
2. `supabase migration list --linked` — only these two (plus any newer ones) should be pending.
3. `supabase db push`
4. Check: `profiles.fcm_token` is gone and `conversations_created_by_fkey` no longer exists.

### Done when
- [ ] Both migrations show as applied in `migration list --linked`
- [ ] Column and FK are gone in the live DB

### What
Deploy the current `delete-account` function. Live is still v3 from around 2026-10-10.

### Why
v3 returns 409 for creators of groups that still have members and still clears `created_by`. The new code removes only the caller's rows.

### Where
- `supabase/functions/delete-account/`

### Steps
1. Apply the two pending migrations first (the new code expects the FK to be gone).
2. `supabase functions deploy delete-account`
3. `supabase functions list` shows a new version.

### Done when
- [ ] New version is live
- [ ] Deleting a test account returns 200
Device test: delete a group creator account with members left

### What
On a device, delete a throwaway account that created a group with other members still in it.

### Why
Confirms SEC-12 end to end: the others keep the group and its history.

### Where
- Settings → Delete account
- `supabase/functions/delete-account/`

### Steps
1. Account A creates a group with B and C and sends a few messages.
2. A deletes the account (goes through the identity check).
3. B and C: the group is still there, messages still decrypt, also on a fresh install after key sync.
4. Also: a DM where both sides delete → the conversation is removed.

### Done when
- [ ] Group survives for remaining members
- [ ] No 409 and no error shown to A

### What
Make `delete-account` refuse unless the caller signed in recently (e.g. JWT `iat` / `auth.sessions` within a few minutes), or require the password in the request.

### Why
The PIN/biometric gate is in the app only. A stolen access token used outside the app can still delete the account.

### Where
- `supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts`
- `utility/account/deleteAccount.ts`
- `utility/auth/verifyAccountPassword`

### Steps
1. Pick the check: recent `last_sign_in_at` vs password re-check in the function.
2. Implement it, return 401 with a clear message when too old.
3. In the app, re-sign-in with the password before calling when needed.
4. Add a test (Deno or pgTAP) for the refusal.

### Done when
- [ ] An old token cannot delete the account
- [ ] Normal in-app deletion still works

tasks: Group creation, rename and group avatar (ChatRoomEditing)
Chat list with last message preview and search
Delete chat from the chat list
Group name changes show live for every member (no refresh)

### What
When a member renames a group, the new name should appear right away for everyone who has the group open or is on the chat list.

### Why
Today other members only see the new name after a refresh. Nothing listens for changes to the `conversations` table: the chat room subscribes to `messages` only, and the chat list to `conversation_participants` only.

### Where
- `app/tabs/msg/[room_id].tsx` (realtime channel around line 271, header title)
- `utility/messages.ts` (`user-conversations:<userId>` channel around line 800, used by the chat list)
- `app/tabs/msg/ChatRoomEditing.tsx` (where the rename is saved)
- new migration in `supabase/migrations/` (realtime publication)

### Steps
1. Migration: `alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.conversations;` (check first that it isn't already in the publication on the live project).
2. Room screen: add an `UPDATE` listener on `conversations` filtered by `id=eq.<conversation_id>` and update the header name (and avatar) from the payload.
3. Chat list: listen for `UPDATE` on `conversations` the user is in (filter by the ids already loaded, or re-fetch the row when an event arrives) and update that row's name.
4. Check the existing `conversations` SELECT policy: realtime only sends rows the member can read, so outsiders get nothing.
5. Test on two simulators: A renames, B sees it in the open room and on the chat list without refreshing.

### Done when
- [ ] B sees the new name within a couple of seconds, in the room header and on the chat list
- [ ] Non-members get no event
- [ ] Migration applied live

epics.title: End-to-end Encryption
epics.summary: Identity keys, conversation keys, encrypted attachments and peer key trust.

stories.title: Own a private identity key on my device

tasks: X25519 key pair on registration, SecureStore per user

stories.title: Encrypt every conversation with its own key
stories.story: As a user, I want each chat to use its own key wrapped for each member, so that one leaked key exposes one chat only.
tasks: Per-conversation ChaCha20-Poly1305 key wrapped per participant
Keyless new device no longer creates orphan chats
Two-device check of the key divergence fix

### What
Verify on two devices that opening a chat from a different entry point no longer re-keys it.

### Why
The 2026-09-17 fix stopped a path that minted a new conversation key and split the thread.

### Where
- `utility/securedMessage/ConversationKeyResolver.ts`
- `app/tabs/(tabs)/Chat.tsx`

### Steps
1. Fresh accounts A and B. A taps B in the avatar list and sends.
2. B opens from the chat list and reads it.
3. B taps A in the avatar list: the thread still decrypts both ways.
4. B deletes the chat, reopens via A's avatar: B recovers its key, A reads every message.

### Done when
- [ ] No 'Key unwrapping failed' anywhere
- [ ] Single thread on both devices
Resolve legacy conversations that still cannot be opened

### What
Some conversations created before the 2026-09-17 key fixes fail with `no candidate public key could unwrap this row`. Find the cause and pick a remedy.

### Why
This is old data, not a current logic bug. Fresh accounts work.

### Where
- `utility/securedMessage/ConversationKeyResolver.ts`
- `app/Bootstrap.tsx` (identity key guard)

### Steps
1. Reproduce on an affected account. The deciding check: does the key derived from this device's private key match that user's `profiles.public_key`?
2. If they differ → a keypair changed after the chat was made; no client fallback can fix it.
3. Choose: (a) accept and document that those chats must be recreated, (b) build a re-share flow where a member who still has the key re-wraps it.

### Done when
- [ ] Cause confirmed
- [ ] Remedy chosen and done (or documented as won't fix)

stories.title: Detect changed peer keys
stories.story: As a user, I want to be warned when a contact's key changes, so that a server-side key swap cannot read my chats.
tasks: Trust-on-first-use peer key pins and 'Security key changed' dialog (SEC-7)
Pin group keys to the wrapping member (`wrapped_by`, SEC-22)

### What
Record who wrapped each conversation-key row (`wrapped_by`) and check the pin against that member, not `conversations.created_by`.

### Why
A row backfilled by another member is checked against the creator's pin, giving a false "key changed" dialog or pinning the wrong key.

### Where
- `utility/securedMessage/ConversationKeyResolver.ts` (`findKeyWrapperPeerId`)
- `backfillMissingWrappedKeys`
- new migration on `conversation_participants`

### Steps
1. Migration: add `wrapped_by uuid` (nullable), RLS so it must equal `auth.uid()` on write.
2. Write it on every wrap and backfill.
3. Resolver: use `wrapped_by` when present, fall back to `created_by`.
4. Unit tests + pgTAP check.

### Done when
- [ ] Backfilled rows no longer trigger a false warning
- [ ] Tests pass
Per-sender message signatures inside a conversation (SEC-8c)

### What
Sign each message with a per-user signing key so members can tell who really sent it.

### Why
All members share one symmetric key, so the AEAD tag only proves "some member sent this". A member could forge another member's message.

### Where
- `utility/securedMessage/ConversationKeyManagement.ts` (documents the limitation)
- `secured.ts`
- `messages` table (new signature column)

### Steps
1. Design: Ed25519 key per user, published like `public_key` and pinned like SEC-7.
2. Sign `(conversation_id, sender_id, nonce, ciphertext)`; verify on read and show a warning on failure.
3. Forwarding re-signs as the forwarder.
4. Migration + tests.

### Done when
- [ ] Forged sender shows a warning
- [ ] Old unsigned messages still display

Add a confirmation step to the remote pairing flow (SEC-23)

### What
Add an explicit confirmation step to remote (server-relayed) pairing, so a new device only gets keys after the user confirms on a device they already trust. Severity: Low.

### Why
The remote flow has no confirmation step. Whoever controls the session or the server could push a pairing through without the user noticing. The local QR flow has the pairing check for this; the remote flow needs its equivalent.

### Where
- `supabase/functions/device-pairing/index.ts`
- `utility/securedMessage/RemoteDevicePairing.ts`, `DeviceIdentity.ts`
- the remote pairing screens (not built yet)

### Steps
1. **Parked until the remote pairing screens exist.** Nothing in `app/` or `components/` uses `RemoteDevicePairing` yet.
2. When the old-device approval screen is built: show the request (device name, time) and a short code or check value derived from the new device's one-time key, the same way the local flow shows a pairing check.
3. Require the user to confirm on the old device, behind the identity check (PIN/biometrics), before `approve()` runs.

Members can only update a conversation's name and avatar (SEC-31)

### What
Limit what a member can change on a `conversations` row to `name` and `avatar_url`. Severity: Low. Found 2026-11-26.

### Why
The UPDATE policy "Allow users update own conversations" only checks membership (`USING`, no `WITH CHECK`), and `authenticated` has `GRANT ALL` on the table. So any member can set `created_by` to anyone or flip `is_group`.

`created_by` is still trusted in two places: the key-wrapper fallback in `findKeyWrapperPeerId` (used when `wrapped_by` is null, e.g. legacy rows) and `delete-account`'s `.eq("created_by", userId)`. Flipping `is_group` changes how clients name the chat and resolve its keys.

### Where
- `supabase/migrations/20260925000000_baseline_schema.sql:842` (policy), `:1093-1094` (grants)
- `utility/securedMessage/ConversationKeyResolver.ts:48` (`findKeyWrapperPeerId`)
- `supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts:68`
- new migration in `supabase/migrations/`, new pgTAP test in `supabase/tests/`

### Steps
1. Check that no client code or RPC updates other `conversations` columns as `authenticated` (grep `.from('conversations').update`, and RPCs that aren't SECURITY DEFINER).
2. Migration: `revoke update on public.conversations from authenticated, anon;` then `grant update (name, avatar_url) on public.conversations to authenticated;`
3. pgTAP: a member can rename and change the avatar; a member can't change `created_by` or `is_group`; an outsider can't update at all.
4. `supabase test db` (all suites), then apply live with `supabase db push`.
5. In the app: renaming a group and changing its avatar still work, and #176's live rename still arrives.

### Done when
- [ ] Only `name` and `avatar_url` can be updated by members
- [ ] New pgTAP checks pass with the other suites
- [ ] Migration applied live
- [ ] security-scan.md #31 marked fixed
